vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: link-digest
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is suspicious due to the direct execution of shell commands (`git add <kb_dir> && git commit ...`) in SKILL.md. While the stated purpose of managing a local knowledge base is benign, the inclusion of a user-configurable variable (`<kb_dir>`) directly into a shell command creates a significant shell injection vulnerability. If the `KB_DIR` variable were to be controlled by an attacker (e.g., via prompt injection into the agent's configuration), it could lead to arbitrary command execution on the host system. This represents a high-risk capability without explicit malicious intent within the skill itself.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions and required actions are consistent with its stated purpose (processing links from a Discord channel, posting a thread, and saving notes); it does not request unrelated credentials or installs, but it will read channel messages, fetch external URLs, write to a local knowledge base, and commit to a git repo, so the user should confirm those resources are safe to use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (process links from a designated Discord channel, summarize, post thread, save KB notes) matches the instructions. The actions the skill requires (reading the channel, fetching URLs, creating Discord threads, writing KB files, and committing to git) are all coherent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to: fetch a URL (web_fetch/web_search), analyze and produce a short summary, create a Discord thread using the platform message API, append a markdown entry to a local KB directory, and run git add/commit. This stays within the declared workflow, but it does grant the skill the ability to read messages from the configured channel and to write/modify files and commits in the repository — verify that only intended channels and KB locations are used and that no sensitive content will be captured.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec, no downloaded code, and no external packages required. Lowest install-risk profile.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md expects configuration values (INTERESTING_FINDING_CHANNEL_ID, KB_DIR) to be set in AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md, but the registry metadata lists no required env vars or credentials. This is proportionate to its function. However, the skill will write to KB_DIR and run git commands — so it implicitly requires filesystem write access and a git environment (author identity or push rights if pushing is added later). Confirm KB_DIR is pointed at an appropriate repository and that no secrets are stored there.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill modifies local files (appends KB entries) and commits changes, and it can create threads in Discord via the platform connector. These privileges are consistent with its purpose but do alter local state and post externally — ensure you want an automated process to create threads and commit to the target repo.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: read a configured Discord channel, fetch and summarize links, post a short analysis in a thread, and add a markdown note to a local KB repo with a git commit. Before installing, verify: (1) the INTERESTING_FINDING_CHANNEL_ID will point only to a channel you trust (so the agent doesn't ingest sensitive messages); (2) KB_DIR is a safe repository/location where automated commits are acceptable; (3) your git identity and repo permissions are set as you expect (the skill will run git add/commit); (4) web_fetch and Discord connectors provided to the agent are authorized and limited appropriately. If you want extra safety: test in a disposable channel/repo first, and require human review of commits or thread posts until you're confident.
